target_customer: Biomanufacturers and synthetic biology developers needing control or containment of engineered organisms
problem: Engineered organisms need reliable ON-OFF control and biocontainment so synthetic biology can be used outside the lab and to optimize production.
business_model: licensing and R&D contracts for protein switch technology, funded largely by grants

founders.name: Gabriel Lopez
founders.background_notes: SynBioBeta article (byline June 2018) says the technology grew out of his Berkeley doctoral research. Source: https://www.synbiobeta.com/read/programmed-for-safety-how-synvivia-is-commercializing-biocontainment-technology

technical_complexity.rationale: Genetically encoded ligand-dependent protein switches with escape rates near 1 in 10^8 cells is research-grade biology.

defensibility.rationale: Technology derived from doctoral research with university IP; rivals use different containment strategies.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying found; the company remains a small active firm.

market_need_then: The SynBioBeta article says containment is needed to use engineered organisms outside the lab; no dated 2016 spend data was found.

identity.logo: logo only on site, not described

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand evidence; sources are a Product Hunt launch in 2018 and a trade article.

outcome_analysis: Synvivia commercializes protein switches that control engineered cells from a Berkeley PhD, remains listed as active with a team of 4 and shows no acquisition or shutdown. Public funding information is limited to aggregator listings and grants, so the company looks like a small grant-supported deep tech startup without a visible venture round; the cause of limited visibility is not public.
notes: No round recorded: aggregators conflict (CB Insights about $730K over five rounds including a Dec 2021 grant; Seedtable one $120K seed Aug 2016; VCBacked names NSF, Creative Ventures, For Good Ventures, California Innovation Fund; ConductScience lists an NIH grant of $856.3K for FY2026) and none was verified against a primary source. Founding year is disputed (2016 vs a 2021 Berkeley incubation). Competition empty: the SynBioBeta article names no competitors and no dated rival source was found. SynBioBeta page metadata date conflicts with the June 2018 byline. YC page says founded in San Francisco, other pages Berkeley.
